---
title: "Troubleshooting"
description: "Every problem I hit while setting up R in VS Code on two Windows machines, with the cause and the fix."
date-format: long
date-modified: last-modified
---

Each entry: the symptom as you see it, the cause, the fix.

## The R terminal closes with exit code -1, or `radian` "is not recognized"

> The terminal process "...\\python.exe -m radian ..." terminated with exit code: -1.

**Cause:** VS Code, and every terminal it opens, keeps the `PATH` from when VS Code was started. If you installed Python, radian or R (or changed `PATH`) while VS Code was running, it does not see them yet. *Developer: Reload Window* does **not** refresh `PATH`.

**Fix:** quit **every** VS Code window, then start VS Code again. Check in a new terminal with `Get-Command radian`.

## radian or VS Code starts an old R version {#radian-or-vs-code-starts-an-old-r-version}

`rig default` says 4.6.2, but `radian --version` or `R.version.string` shows an older R.

**Cause:** something pins R before rig gets a say. In order of how often I met them:

1. an `R_HOME` environment variable. It can be a **user** variable as well as a system one;
2. a version folder such as `C:\Program Files\R\R-4.5.0\bin` on `PATH`, usually left by an old installer or a tutorial;
3. a workspace `.vscode/settings.json` with `r.executablePath` or `--r-binary` (that one is on purpose, see [R versions](r_versions.qmd#pin-one-project-to-a-version)).

**Fix:** remove `R_HOME` (*System Properties → Environment Variables*, check both lists), remove the version folder from `PATH`, restart VS Code. The [PATH check](outside_vscode.qmd#path-rules) shows what a new process will see.

## "Backend 'lintr' requires lintr >= 3.3.0-1"

> Backend 'lintr' requires lintr >= 3.3.0-1. Install it or select another backend.

The R terminal may also not finish loading.

**Cause:** vscode-R 3.3 lints through lintr and needs a recent version. Packages are per R version, so a version you have not used for a while still has the old lintr.

**Fix:** `install.packages("lintr")` **in the R version that is active**, then restart VS Code (or the R language server).

## Red or struck-through R settings {#old-r-setting-names}

**Cause:** vscode-R 3.x renamed several settings. The old names still work but are deprecated:

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `r.rterm.windows` | `r.consolePath` |
| `r.rterm.option` | `r.consoleArgs` |
| `r.rpath.windows` | `r.executablePath` |
| `r.rtermSendDelay` | `r.consoleSendDelay` |
| `r.plot.useHttpgd` | `r.plot.backend` (`"httpgd"`) |

**Fix:** rename them, and take the chance to remove absolute paths: see [How VS Code finds R](r_versions.qmd#how-vs-code-finds-r). Check **every** profile, including Default: profiles do not inherit, so an old entry can hide in one of them.

## A setting changed on one machine never arrives on the other

**Cause:** Settings Sync silently skips machine-scoped settings, and several vscode-R settings are machine-scoped.

**Fix:** the `settingsSync.ignoredSettings` list with a `-` prefix, in the Default profile and in each synced profile. Details in [the gotcha](profiles_sync.qmd#the-gotcha).

## `rig add release` hangs with no output

**Cause:** it waits for the Windows administrator (UAC) prompt, which may be behind other windows.

**Fix:** find and accept the prompt. If rig fails at once with "The operation was canceled by the user", it could not show the prompt (this happens when it is started from a non-interactive shell, such as a coding agent's terminal): run it in a normal or elevated PowerShell window.

## `rig` is not found right after installing it

**Cause:** the terminal was opened before rig was added to `PATH`.

**Fix:** open a new terminal.

## winget fails to install Rtools: "Target directory already exists"

> Target directory already exists: C:\\rtools45. Please remove previous installation or select another location.

**Cause:** Rtools 4.5 is already installed, just not through winget, so winget does not know about it.

**Fix:** none needed if R finds it: `pkgbuild::has_build_tools()` is `TRUE` and `Sys.which("make")` points into `C:\rtools45`.

## R uses an old Quarto after upgrading Quarto

`quarto --version` in PowerShell shows the new version, but rendering from R uses the old one.

**Cause:** `QUARTO_PATH`, or a `PATH` entry for an older per-user Quarto, set in a `.Rprofile`.

**Fix:** remove them, so that R finds Quarto on `PATH` (see [.Rprofile](outside_vscode.qmd#rprofile)). Then uninstall the old copy.

## Errors at every R start-up, or settings from the wrong `.Rprofile`

> Error in loadNamespace(x) : there is no package called 'btw'

**Cause:** either a `.Rprofile` calls a package that this R version does not have (each R version has its own library), or R reads a different `.Rprofile` than you think: one in the current folder wins over the one in `Documents`.

**Fix:** guard optional packages with `requireNamespace("pkg", quietly = TRUE)`, and keep only one user `.Rprofile` ([details](outside_vscode.qmd#rprofile)).

## `radian` installs but crashes or will not start

**Cause:** usually a Python version radian does not support yet, or a second Python earlier on `PATH`.

**Fix:** use Python 3.12 and make sure it comes first on `PATH`: `Get-Command python, radian` must both point to `Python312`. If `pip install radian` fails while compiling, install the [Microsoft C++ Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/).

## Plots open in a separate window, not in VS Code

**Cause:** httpgd is not installed for the active R version, so the `.Rprofile` and vscode-R fall back to the standard Windows graphics device.

**Fix:** `install.packages("httpgd")`, then restart the R terminal.
